Subject: Discovery recap — migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Shoply)

Hi Oliver / Priya —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve attached a short recap + a compatibility checklist we’ll use for the PoC.

Pain points you called out:
- Cost pressure: current spend on OpenAI/Anthropic for generation and embeddings has grown month-over-month and is unpredictable.
- Latency & tail spikes: occasional 500-1200ms token latency affecting feature X (bot responses + search re-rank).
- Vendor lock & compliance: need the option to run inference in a VPC/on-prem for regulated customers and to meet data residency requirements.
- Model compatibility: your product uses function/tool-calling, structured JSON outputs, and embeddings for semantic search - replacement models must be compatible.

Current stack (from call):
- Generation / chat: OpenAI GPT-4.1 via API (business-critical flows).
- Safety / guardrails: Anthropic for assistant moderation in a subset of traffic.
- Embeddings: OpenAI/embeddings endpoint for search and similarity detections.
- Backend: Node.js microservices + Redis for short-term KV cache + PostgreSQL.

Success criteria you defined:
- Cost: target >= 30-40% reduction in unit inference cost (tokens/embedding) at production volume.
- Latency: P50 < 150ms for short prompts, P95 < 400ms; tail improvements for realtime features.
- Compatibility: support for instruction-following, tool/function calling, and embeddings parity within an acceptable delta in semantic search relevance.
- Deployment: ability to run in a Dedicated or Private deployment (VPC) with KMS integration and audit logs.

Shortlist & initial technical considerations (high level):
- Models to evaluate: Llama 3 variants (13B, 34B), Mistral-Instruct, Falcon-180B-instruct distilled, and open embedding models (e.g., Llama-2 embeddings alternatives / open-embedding variants).
- Quantization: 4-bit/8-bit quantization options to balance cost and perf for your throughput.
- Tooling: function-calling surface and stable response formats - we’ll run prompt/response parity tests against your existing templates.

Immediate next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (SE-led) - 60m session next week to review sample prompts, the embedding evaluation set, and SLOs. (Action: Aditya to schedule)
2) Model compatibility tests - Rishi will run initial microbenchmarks on suggested models and share results.
3) PoC scope & timeline - Marissa to share a PoC template + SOW draft and pricing options for Dedicated vs. Hosted fallback.
4) Procurement / security questionnaire - Priya to share procurement windows and any specific legal / SOC 2 evidence needed.

Attachments: redwood-discovery-recap.pdf (this recap), model-compatibility-checklist.xlsx (checklist + sample evaluation matrix).

If anything above needs correction, flag it and I’ll update. If this looks right, Aditya will send a calendar invite for the SE deep-dive.

Thanks again,

Marissa Cole

Thanks for the clear recap - this matches our notes. A couple of clarifications / priorities from our side:
- Embeddings parity is the highest-risk item for search relevance - we’ll need a small labeled set (I can share ~200 queries + expected top-5).
- Latency targets are softer on batch offline generation, but strict for chat/assistant flows where customers notice delays.
- Security: must have KMS integration and the ability to audit inference logs for requests touching PII.

We’re good to proceed with the SE deep-dive. Priya - procurement would like to know typical lead times for Dedicated capacity (order-to-live) and any minimum commitments.
